title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 178A (Pledge by person in possession under voidable contract)

content.overview: Section 178A provides that when the pawnor has obtained possession of the goods pledged by him under a contract voidable under section 19 or section 19A, but the contract has not been rescinded at the time of the pledge, the pawnee acquires a good title to the goods, provided he acts in good faith and without notice of the pawnor's defect of title.
content.glance: Pawnee acquires good title if the pawnor obtained possession under a voidable contract (ss. 19 or 19A) that has not been rescinded at the time of the pledge, provided the pawnee acts in good faith without notice of the defect of title.
content.study: When the pawnor has obtained possession of the goods pledged by him under a contract voidable under section 19 or section 19A, but the contract has not been rescinded at the time of the pledge, the pawnee acquires a good title to the goods, provided he acts in good faith and without notice of the pawnor's defect of title. Current-law framing: protects good-faith pawnees where the voidable contract has not yet been avoided.

examples.title: Voidable contract not rescinded
examples.body: Pawnor obtained goods under a voidable contract not yet rescinded and pledges them to a good-faith pawnee without notice. Pawnee acquires good title under Section 178A.

hypotheticals.question: Pawnor obtained possession under a voidable contract that has not been rescinded. Does a good-faith pawnee without notice get good title?
